title: Builder Sponsorship — application
description: Question labels are load-bearing. The webhook parser identifies fields by matching words in the label against the alias tables in talent_engine/ingest/normalize.py, so renaming a question can silently stop a field being read. tests/test_form_spec.py round-trips this file through the parser and fails if any mapped question stops resolving. Change labels here, not in Tally's editor.

questions.label: Your name
questions.why: Quarantined. Never enters an assessment record.

questions.label: Email
questions.why: Quarantined. How you tell someone they were selected.

questions.label: Telegram handle
questions.why: Quarantined. Matches HANDLE_KEYS on the word 'handle', which is why the parser skips contact-labelled fields when looking for the GitHub login.

questions.label: GitHub username
questions.why: The only field the automated score depends on. A response without a usable one is stored for human review, never zero-scored.

questions.label: Which repo should we look at first?
questions.why: Monitored during the program to see whether the funded work actually moves.

questions.label: Build plan — what will you make with this sponsorship?
questions.why: Collected and shown to reviewers, deliberately unscored. The overlay requires it for selection; scoring free text would make the rubric unreproducible.

questions.label: How does this connect to Celo?
questions.why: Program fit, assessed by a human at selection and again at the month-two gate. Not a scored dimension — fit is a program question, not an evidence question.

questions.label: Referred by
questions.why: Scores only on exact match against the program's registry. An unrecognised name scores zero and flags — so leave it blank rather than guessing.

questions.label: Which of these factors apply to you?
options: No local technology industry where I live
questions.why: Self-declared only. Invariant 2: nothing about a person's circumstances is ever inferred. Tally sends option ids, not text — the parser resolves them, or these would score as unrecognised factors.

questions.label: Anything about your context we should know?
questions.why: Capped by the rubric weight and disabled entirely for recruitment-mode programs. Self-declared and unverifiable by design.

questions.label: Do you accept the sponsorship terms?
options: I have read the terms at sponsorships.prezenti.xyz and I accept them: Claude Max 20x, ChatGPT Pro 5x and allowance support; 2% of revenue actually received by the product through Celo, and any grant, prize and retro-funding income won with the sponsored work. This is owed to Prezenti and to nobody else, capped at $14,000, expiring 36 months after the term, pro-rated by the months I receive, and paid directly to the verified Prezenti Safe. I must post monthly public updates; 30 days inactive triggers review with a 7-day cure period; months three and four require a month-two Celo deployment, integration or material contribution. No equity is taken. I keep all IP and may withdraw at any time without penalty. I understand acceptance requires a public Celo EAS pledge that names my GitHub handle. [terms-version: {terms_digest}]
questions.why: Terms displayed on a page are not agreement; an affirmative act is. The option text restates the substance, including benefits, covered income, monitoring conditions, the month-two continuation gate, direct payment to the Prezenti Safe and the mandatory public on-chain pledge, so nobody accepts a link they did not open. It carries the digest of the terms it was written against. A ticked checkbox is submitted as its own option text, so the applicant transmits the version they actually saw — Tally has no API for hidden fields, and stamping the server's current digest when the webhook arrives recorded acceptance of words a stale form never showed. Changing the terms changes the digest, which changes this text, which is exactly the re-consent that should be required.
